blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en:
Large Language Model (LLM) agents now take part in organizational work, where many authors record decisions across documents over months.
Because a revised decision arrives as a new document rather than an edit, answering a question requires knowing which version held at a given time.
However, most memory systems compress the record at write time.
By distilling each document into facts, notes or graph edges, these methods fix what can be answered before any question is asked.
To address this, we propose Mem++, a non-destructive memory framework shifting from write-time distillation to read-time selection.
Mem++ stores every document whole with its date and author, and it calls no generative model at write time.
At read time, it retrieves only documents dated up to the time a question asks about and fuses lexical and semantic rankings.
Unlike systems that overwrite older versions, Mem++ keeps them and leaves the choice to the answering model.
Evaluations on the organizational benchmark OrgMemBench demonstrate that Mem++ surpasses the strongest memory system baseline by 8.0 to 13.1 points across two answering models.
With gpt-4.1-mini, it also achieves the best overall score, 2.6 points above RAG.
In addition, Mem++ achieves the best average LLM-judge score on LoCoMo and ranks second on LongMemEval S {}_{\text{S}} , behind only its entity-graph variant.
Code for benchmark evaluation is available at https://github.com/AIDAChip-Inc/mem-plus-plus
blocks.zh:
大型语文模型代理人现在参加组织工作,许多作者在几个月内记录了各种文件的决定。
由于订正决定是作为新文件而不是编辑而提出的,回答一个问题需要知道在特定时间持有哪个版本。
然而,大多数内存系统在写时都会压缩记录.
通过将每份文件提炼成事实、注释或图表边缘,这些方法可以确定在提出问题之前可以回答的问题。
为了解决这个问题,我们提议Mem++,一个无损的内存框架,从写时蒸馏转向读时选择.
Mem++将每个文档的全文都存有其日期和作者,在写作时它不称为基因模型.
在阅读时,它只检索到一个问题提出之前的文件,并将词汇和语义的排名联系起来。
与覆盖旧版本的系统不同,Mem++保留了这些版本,并将选择权留给解答模式.
对组织基准OrgMem Bench的评价表明,Mem++在两个答题模型中超过最强的内存系统基线8.0至13.1分.
凭借gpt-4.1-mini,它也取得了最好的总分,比RAG高2.6分.
此外,Mem++在LoCoMo上实现了最佳平均LLM评分,并在LongMemEval S QQText{S}}上排名第二,仅次于其实体图变体.

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en:
Large Language Model (LLM) agents now take part in organizational work, from daily tasks to decisions that span many teams over months ( Kirchdorfer et al., 2026 ) . Such critical work is only possible if the agent can correctly recall what was already decided ( Zeng et al., 2025 ) . In an organization, the record of past decisions is shared; organizational memory keeps the history that informs present decisions ( Walsh and Ungson, 1991 ) , and it is written by humans and agents alike.
To have a deeper understanding of the context and intent of the organization, a shared memory that mixes agents, humans, and compound their knowledge becomes a necessity.
blocks.zh:
大型语言模型(LLM)代理人现在参与组织工作,从日常任务到跨越多个团队数月的决定(Kirchdorfer等人,2026年). 只有代理人能够正确回忆已经作出的决定(Zeng等人,2025年),这种关键的工作才有可能。 在一个组织中,过去决定的记录是共享的;组织记忆保存着为当前决定提供依据的历史(Walsh和Ungson,1991年),它由人类和代理人共同撰写.
为了更深入地了解组织的背景和意图,必须有一个将代理人、人类和复合其知识的共同记忆。

blocks.en:
Organizational memory differs from the conversational, single-agent memory that existing systems were built for ( Figure 1 ).
Conversational memory has a single dialogue whose statements accumulate rather than compete, and a later statement is therefore read as an update of an earlier one.
Organizational memory, in contrast, is written by many people independently of one another across email, tickets, meeting notes and shared documents ( Gardner, 2026 ) .
Moreover, a decision that changes an earlier one is written as a new document rather than as an edit to the old one.
For example, a policy set in March, revised in June and reversed in September exists as three documents, and all three remain because nobody goes back to remove them.
Consequently, answering a question against this record takes more than finding the most recent version.
Conversational memory struggles here, because they treat every statement as coming from the same authority.
For example, Mem0 ( Chhikara et al., 2025 ) resolves the conflict by overwriting, so the approved decision is replaced by the proposal and can no longer be retrieved afterwards.
In addition, Zep ( Rasmussen et al., 2025 ) keeps both statements, because its Graphiti engine stamps every edge with the valid period, but it stores extracted facts rather than the documents.
blocks.zh:
组织内存不同于现有系统是为对话而建的单一代理内存(图1)。
对话记忆有一个单一的对话,其语句累积而非竞争,因此后期语句被解读为前期语句的更新.
而组织记忆则由许多人独立书写,
此外,改变先前的决定是作为新文件而不是作为编辑旧文件而写成的。
例如,3月制定、6月修订、9月倒置的政策作为三份文件存在,所有三份文件都保留下来,因为没有人回去删除这些文件。
因此,回答对这一记录提出的问题,需要的不仅仅是找到最新版本。
对话性的记忆力在这里挣扎,因为他们把每个陈述都视为来自同一个权威.
例如,Mem0(Chhikara等人,2025年)通过覆写解决了冲突,因此批准的决定被提案所取代,此后无法再检索.

blocks.en:
Existing memory systems resolve one trade-off at ingest, between keeping the record and structuring it.
Traditional retrieval-based systems keep the raw text and search it by similarity ( Packer et al., 2023 ) , and nothing is discarded, but nothing is organized either.
A query, therefore, cannot distinguish a superseded value from one still in force.
This is how the memory stream of generative agents works, appending each observation in its original form and retrieving it later by relevance and recency ( Park et al., 2023 ) .
Structured systems make the opposite choice. They record how statements relate to one another at ingest, and the raw text does not survive that step.
For instance, Mem0 stores a set of facts ( Chhikara et al., 2025 ) , Zep a graph of dated edges ( Rasmussen et al., 2025 ) , and HippoRAG and GraphRAG an entity graph extracted from the corpus ( Gutiérrez et al., 2024 ; Edge et al., 2024 ) , and in none of them does a later query reach the document itself.
A memo that changes a decision is reduced to a relation between an entity and a value.
Its reason, condition and approval are not entity-shaped, and they never enter the store.
What will be answerable is therefore fixed before any question has been asked.
As we show in Section 4 , this explains the sharp drop of conversational memory systems on OrgMemBench, a benchmark of multi-author temporal, contradiction and justification-chain questions that define organizational memory.
blocks.zh:
现有的内存系统在保存记录和安排记录之间解决一个取舍。
传统的基于检索的系统保存原始文本,并通过相似性进行搜索(Packer等人,2023年),没有东西被丢弃,但也没有组织起来.
因此,查询无法区分被取代的价值和仍然有效的价值。
基因剂的记忆流就是这样工作的,将每个观测结果以原始形式附后,然后通过相关性和再生性加以检索(Park等人,2023年).
结构化系统作出相反的选择。 它们记录了发言如何相互交织在一起,原始文本也未能幸存下来。
例如,Mem0存储了一组事实(Chhikara等人,2025年),Zep存储了一张日期边缘图(Rasmussen等人,2025年),以及HippoRAG和GraphRAG存储了从该文书中提取的实体图(Gutiérrez等人,2024年;Edge等人,2024年),其中没有任何一个后来查询到文件本身。

它的原因,条件和批准不是实体形状的,他们从不进入商店.
因此,在提出任何问题之前,将回答什么问题。
正如我们在第4节中所表明的那样,这解释了OrgMem Bench上对话记忆系统急剧下降的原因,OrgMem Bench是界定组织记忆的多作者时间、矛盾和理由链问题的基准。

blocks.en:
To address these limitations we introduce Mem++ , an organizational memory architecture that moves the decision about what matters from write time to read time.
(i) Every artifact is stored whole and remains the unit of retrieval.
(ii) Structure can be added as an optional layer over the retained documents rather than as a replacement for them.
A Mem++ pass groups near-duplicates and marks older conflicting versions as superseded without deleting them, and we evaluate it as an ablation.
(iii) Selection is deferred until a question arrives, and it therefore ranges over the full record rather than a pruned set of facts.
What distinguishes Mem++ is therefore not that the record is kept, but that each document stays whole with its date and the choice between versions is made at read time.
Our contributions are as follows:

(二) 可增加结构,作为保留文件的可选层次,而不是替代。

(三) 选择被推迟到提问到来后进行,因此,选择超越了全部记录,而不是一连串被调查的事实。
因此,区分Mem++的不是保存记录,而是每个文档与日期保持完整,并在阅读时选择不同版本。

blocks.en: 2 Related Work
blocks.zh: 2 相关工作

blocks.en: 2.1 Conversational Memory Architectures for LLM Agents
blocks.zh: 2.1 LLM代理的谈话内存架构

blocks.en:
Agent memories give an LLM persistent state beyond its context window, differing in how they carry information across sessions.
MemGPT ( Packer et al., 2023 ) and the generative agents memory ( Park et al., 2023 ) hold the record in full and leave every judgement to retrieval.
Details survives, but nothing marks how one statement stands to another, so a query cannot separate a replaced value from one still activated.
Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) grounds answers in an external corpus by chunking documents, embedding them, and returning the nearest chunks at query time ( Lewis et al., 2020 ; Karpukhin et al., 2020 ) .
However, the words survive while the document does not, since chunking separates a passage from the rest of its text and from any later version of it.
Most recent approaches instead compress at ingest, gaining structure at the cost of the record.
Mem0 distils each document into facts and overwrites them on conflict ( Chhikara et al., 2025 ) .
Similarly, A-Mem, Nemori, LightMem and LiCoMemory rewrite interactions into episodes through clustering, summarization or note-taking ( Xu et al., 2026 ; Nan et al., 2025 ; Fang et al., 2026 ; Huang et al., 2026 ) .
In addition, G-Memory organizes these episodes hierarchically ( Zhang et al., 2026 ) , PREMem reasons as it writes ( Kim et al., 2025 ) , and MemOS exposes memory as a managed layer ( Li et al., 2025 ) .
Each gains a compact store but loses the source and the links between its statements, and what can be answered is fixed at ingest.
In contrast, Mem++ stores every document whole at write time and marks superseded statements with a date instead of deleting them.
This approach keeps every version available and leaves the choice between them to read time, and conflicting statements from different authors therefore remain answerable.
blocks.zh:
代理记忆在其上下文窗口之外给出了LLM的持久性状态,在不同会话间传递信息的方式有所不同.
MemGPT(Packer等人,2023年)和基因剂内存(Park等人,2023年)保存了全部记录,并让每个判断都进行检索.
细节仍然存续,但没有任何东西标出一个语句对另一个语句的立场,因此一个查询不能将一个替换的值与一个仍然激活的值分开.
检索到的生成(RAG)通过对文件进行块化、嵌入和在查询时间返回最近的块来在外部体中解答(Lewis等人,2020年;Karpukhin等人,2020年)。
然而,这些词语仍然存续,而文件却不存续,因为从其他文本和以后任何文本中划出一段。
最近的办法是以摄取方式压缩,以记录为代价增加结构。
Mem0将每份文件归纳为事实,并覆盖关于冲突的事实(Chhikara等人,2025年)。
同样,A-Mem、Nemori、LightMem和LiCoMemory通过集群、归纳或记分将相互作用重写成各集(徐等人,2026年;Nan等人,2025年;Fang等人,2026年;Huang等人,2026年)。
此外,G-Memory还分级组织这些剧集(Zhang et al.,2026),PREMem写作的理由(Kim et al.,2025),MemOS将记忆暴露为一个管理层(Li et al.,2025).
每个都得到一个紧凑的商店,但失去了源头和其语句之间的联系,而能够回答的则固定在摄入状态.
相比之下,Mem++在写时存储每个文件的完整内容,并标记用日期代替语句而不是删除.
这种方法使每个版本都可以使用,并让它们之间选择阅读时间,因此,不同作者相互矛盾的陈述仍然可以回答.

blocks.en: 2.2 Long-term Temporal Memory Systems
blocks.zh: 2.2 长期时间记忆系统

blocks.en:
Temporal questions ask what held at a given time or what a newer statement replaced, and conversational benchmarks such as LongMemEval and LoCoMo test them through knowledge-update and temporal-reasoning categories ( Wu et al., 2024 ; Maharana et al., 2024 ) .
Existing systems handle such changes in two ways.
The first discards or alters the older value.
For instance, Mem0 overwrites an older fact once a newer one arrives ( Chhikara et al., 2025 ) , A-Mem revises related notes in place when a new one is added ( Xu et al., 2026 ) , and MemoryBank lets older memories fade along a forgetting curve ( Zhong et al., 2024 ) .
The second keeps the older value with a date.
Zep and LongMemEval attach time intervals or timestamps to stored facts so that queries can be bounded by date ( Rasmussen et al., 2025 ; Wu et al., 2024 ) .
In conversational memory, both mechanisms treat a change as one narrator updating their own facts, and the newest value is therefore assumed to be correct while the older one is removed or kept only as history.
In an organization, however, changes arrive as new documents from different authors across different channels, and questions ask about past versions as often as about the current state ( Gardner, 2026 ) .
Mem++ addresses this by keeping every version as a stored document, marking the replaced one with the date it stopped holding.
Then, each retrieval is bounded by the date in the question, which lets one store answer what holds now, what held before, and what changed.
In other terms, it reconstructs the life journey of a fact and how it changed. This is useful for organization to track pivot points in decisions making, allowing the agents and humans to revisit these later.
blocks.zh:
时间问题询问在特定时间持有什么,或更新声明取代什么,以及LongMemEval和LoCoMo等对话基准通过知识和时间推理类别加以检验(Wu等人,2024年;Maharana等人,2024年)。
现有系统以两种方式处理这种变化。
第一批丢弃物或改变旧值。
例如,Mem0在较新的事实出现后就覆盖了更古老的事实(Chhikara等人,2025年),A-Mem在添加新的事实时修改了相关的注释(Xu等人,2026年),记忆银行让更古老的记忆沿着遗忘的曲线消逝(Zhong等人,2024年).
第二则保留较旧的值与日期.
Zep和LongMemEval对存储的事实附加时间间隔或时间戳,以便查询可以按日期进行(Rasmussen等人,2025年;Wu等人,2024年).
在对话记忆中,两种机制都把改变视为一个旁白者更新自己的事实,因此,最新的价值被假定是正确的,而旧的则被删除或仅保留为历史。
然而在一个组织中,随着不同作者通过不同渠道的新文件的到来,变化的到来,质疑过去版本的频率与当前状态(Gardner, 2026 )一样.
Mem++通过保留每个版本作为存储的文档来解决这个问题,用它停止持有的日期标记被替换的文档.
然后,每次检索都以问题中的日期为界,它让一家商店回答现在持有的,之前持有的,以及改变的.
换句话说,它重建了一个事实的人生历程以及它是如何改变的. 这对于组织跟踪决策的中枢点很有用,让代理人和人类日后重新审视这些点.

blocks.en: 3 Method
blocks.zh: 3 方法

blocks.en:
Organizations keep records to preserve their decisions over time ( Walsh and Ungson, 1991 ) .
Unlike a conversation, this record is a stream of dated documents from many authors.
A useful memory must therefore tell what the current value is, what the value was at a past date, and what a change replaced and who made it.
To this end, Mem++ stores each new document whole, never rewrites or deletes one to resolve a conflict, and leaves the choice between versions to the answering model. Figure 2 shows its three stages, namely a write path that stores documents, an optional consolidation pass that links their versions ( Appendix A ), and a read path that answers a question against the store. Algorithm 1 in Appendix A gives the pseudocode.

各组织保存记录,以保存其长期决定(Walsh和Ungson,1991年)。
与谈话不同的是,这张唱片是来自许多作者的一串过时文件.
因此,一个有用的记忆必须说明目前的价值是什么,过去的日期是什么价值,什么变化被取代了,是谁做的。
为此,Mem++存储每个新文档整体,从不重写或删除一个以解决冲突,并将版本之间的选择留给解答模式. 图2显示了其三个阶段,即存储文档的写路径,链接其版本的可选合并通道(附录A),以及解答对商店的质疑的读路径. 附录A中的算法1给出了伪码.

blocks.en: Unlike approaches that segment the stream into windows or rewrite it into extracted units ( Chhikara et al., 2025 ) , the write path stores each document once and as a whole, so no segment boundary splits a document and no model guesses at write time what a later question may need.

Documents longer than the encoder limit are truncated only in 𝐞 \mathbf{e} , while x x and the lexical index keep the full text.

New documents are added without touching the rows already stored.

Adding a document thus costs one embedding, and no older row is reprocessed.

因此,添加一个文档需要嵌入一个文件,没有旧行进行再处理。

At ingest, Mem g ++ extracts entity-relation triples from each document with a language model, and these triples form the graph.
At query time, one model call extracts the entities named in, and the graph is searched from those entities to collect related triples.
These graph results are appended after the fused rows, at most five per question, so Mem g ++ sees more context than the systems it is compared against.
Triples carry no date and the as-of condition is not applied to them, so on a dated question the graph can surface relations from artifacts later than θ \theta .

At write time, two gpt-4o-mini calls extract entity-relation triples from each document, and these triples form the graph 𝒦 \mathcal{K} .
At query time, one model call extracts the entities V q V_{q} named in q q , and 𝒦 \mathcal{K} is searched from those entities to collect related triples.
These triples are appended after the fused rows, at most five per question. This is why on the conversational benchmarks, Mem g ++ sees more context than the systems it is compared against.
The triples carry no date and the as-of condition is not applied to them, so on a dated question the graph can surface relations drawn from documents later than θ \theta .

blocks.en: 3.4 Evidence Presentation
blocks.zh: 3.4 证据列报

blocks.en: Each row is rendered in rank order as its original text preceded by its event date and, where the source records one, an author tag, so that the model can compare versions of a fact by when they were written. On OrgMemBench the header is built from t t and that tag, although no artifact on the reported tier names an author, so every row’s header carries the same placeholder author alongside the date. On the conversational suites the date and speaker already lead the stored text, so each row is shown as stored, preceded only by its rank number. This design keeps Mem++ a memory rather than a reasoner, so it adds no inference step of its own at answer time.
blocks.zh: 每行按顺序排列,作为它的原始文本在事件日期之前,以及当源记录到一个时,一个作者标记,这样模型就可以比较一个事实的版本到写时. 在 OrgMem Bench 上, 标题由 t t 和 标签 组成, 虽然没有作者在报告级别名称上的文物, 在对话套件上,日期和扬声器已经引导了存储的文本,因此每行显示为存储,仅前方显示其排位号. 这种设计保持了Mem++的内存而不是理性,因此在回答时间没有增加自己的推论步骤.

blocks.en: 4 Experiments
blocks.zh: 4 实验

blocks.en: 4.1 Experimental Setup
blocks.zh: 4.1 实验设置

blocks.en:
We evaluate Mem++ on three benchmarks, one organizational and two conversational, which together cover the settings it is Mem++ designed for. OrgMemBench ( Gardner, 2026 ) is our primary benchmark, a synthetic bi-temporal corpus of one fictional organization that we use unmodified.
We run its medium tier, which pairs 443 dated artifacts, organized into 157 threads over 18 months where later decisions revise earlier ones, with 73 questions over six capabilities that range from supersession to contradiction (Figure 3 ).
The question count is small, yet each answer is graded against a rubric rather than marked right or wrong, giving 247 graded facets and a score in [ 0 , 1 ] [0,1] that reflects partial coverage of the expected evidence. LoCoMo ( Maharana et al., 2024 ) provides 10 multi-session dialogues of about 24K tokens each and 1,540 questions across four reasoning categories, and it is the most widely used for memories. LongMemEval S ( Wu et al., 2024 ) keeps a similar question format while spreading each of its 500 questions over roughly 48 sessions and 494 turns, which tests if a memory still holds when the history grows.
blocks.zh:
我们评价Mem++的三个基准,一个是组织基准,两个是对话基准,这些基准共同涵盖Mem++的设计环境。 OrgMem Bench(Gardner, 2026)是我们的首要基准,一个我们使用未经修改的虚构组织的合成双时元体.
我们运行它的中层,共配有443件古董,在18个月内编成157条线,其中后来的决定修改了先前的决定,从超会话到矛盾的6个能力(图3)共73个问题。
问题计数是小的,然而每个答案都是对照一个标题而不是标对错进行分级,给出了247个分级的方面和[0,1][0,1]的分数,反映了对预期证据的部分覆盖. LoCoMo(Maharana等人,2024年)提供10个多会对话,每个约24K令牌和1,540个问题,跨越4个推理类别,它是用于记忆最广泛的. Long MemEval S(Wu et al., 2024)保持类似的问题格式,同时将其500个问题中每个问题分布在大约48个会话和494个转弯上,这测试了历史发展时一个记忆是否仍然保持.

blocks.en:
We benchmark against seven methods that range from no external memory to richly structured ones, namely Full Context (entire history in the prompt), RAG-4096 ( Lewis et al., 2020 , 4096-token chunks for dense retrieval) , Mem0 ( Chhikara et al., 2025 , fact extraction with update and delete rules) , Zep ( Rasmussen et al., 2025 , temporal knowledge graph with dated edges) , A-Mem ( Xu et al., 2026 , structured notes with evolving links) , LangMem ( LangChain AI, 2025 , automatic memory extraction across sessions) , and gbrain ( Gardner, 2026 , entity graph over organizational documents) .
Full Context, RAG-4096, Mem0 and Zep serve as general-purpose baselines and run on all three benchmarks, whereas A-Mem and LangMem, which designed for conversational memory, run only on LoCoMo and LongMemEval S , and gbrain, which was released with OrgMemBench, runs only there.
blocks.zh:
我们参照了从没有外部内存到结构丰富的七种方法,即:全面背景(即时历史),RAG-4096(Lewis等人,2020年,4096-token 块进行密集检索),Mem0(Chhikara等人,2025年,更新和删除规则的事实提取),Zep(Rasmussen等人,2025年,带有日期边缘的时间知识图),A-Mem(Xu等人,2026年,有不断发展的链接的结构图),LangMem(LangChain AI,2025年,跨会自动内存提取),以及gbraine(Gardner,2026年,组织文件的实体图)。
Full Contact,RAG-4096,Mem0和Zep作为通用基线,运行在所有三个基准上,而A-Mem和LangMem为对话记忆设计,只在LoCoMo和LongMemEval S上运行,与OrgMem Bench一起发布的gbrain只运行在那里.

blocks.en:
On all three datasets, our primary evaluation metric is the LLM-judge score (abbreviated as LLM for simplicity), using gpt-4o-mini as the judges.
On LoCoMo and LongMemEval S , we additionally report F1 and BLEU-1 .
For OrgMemBench, the judges grade against the benchmark’s rubric.
For LongMemEval S , prompts are adapted to its task-specific question-answering format, following Zep ( Rasmussen et al., 2025 ) .
These metrics are accuracy metrics of different standard, and are scaled to the 0–100 range, with higher values indicating better performance and 100 denoting a perfect score.

在所有三个数据集上,我们的主要评价尺度是LLM法官得分(简略为LLM),使用gpt-4o-mini作为评委.
在LoCoMo和LongMemEval上 S,我们补充报告F1和BLEU-1。
对OrgMem Bench来说,法官的级别比基准的级别高。
朗梅瓦尔 S, 提示按其特定任务问答格式调整, 沿用Zep(Rasmussen等人, 2025年).
这些度量衡是不同标准的精度度度量,被缩放到0–100范围内,更高的值表明性能更好,100表示一个完美的分数.

blocks.en:
To ensure fair comparison, Mem0 and Zep retrieve memory contexts, which are then fed to gpt-4o-mini, gpt-4.1-mini for answer generation.
All other methods, including Mem++, employ the same models for answer generation, while Mem g ++ uses gpt-4o-mini as its internal graph backbone.
All retrieval-based baselines employ the powerful text-embedding-3-small model, whereas Mem++ uses the lightweight all-MiniLM-L6-v2 model. The lexical index matches query terms disjunctively by default and conjunctively on OrgMemBench.
Key hyperparameters are the fusion constant γ \gamma and the pathway weights w ℓ w_{\ell} , while the consolidation threshold τ \tau applies only when consolidation is enabled.
For retrieval count, we fix k = 50 k=50 in main experiments, while k k varies from 10 to 100 in the ablation study, as shown in the Appendix.

Regarding these tables, we highlight the following observations.

blocks.en:
Strong Performance on Organizational Memory. Mem++ achieves the best overall score on OrgMemBench with gpt-4.1-mini, reaching 57.6 and surpassing the strongest baseline, RAG, by 2.6 points.
With gpt-4o-mini, Mem g ++ and Mem++ rank first and second with 44.4 and 44.2, ahead of RAG at 43.4.
The memory systems fall further behind, and Mem++ exceeds the best of them by 13.1 points over A-Mem with gpt-4.1-mini and by 8.0 points over Zep with gpt-4o-mini.
Full Context performs worst, scoring below 18 overall and near zero on Supersession and Bi-temporal questions with both answerers.
This suggests that placing the whole record in context does not by itself reveal which version holds.

We attribute the gap over Mem0 and Zep to keeping every original document in the store with its date and author.
In contrast, Mem0 overwrites a fact on conflict, which likely explains its Supersession scores of 40.8 and 32.3.

blocks.en:
Competitive Performance on Conversational Memory. Although Mem++ targets organizational records, it also achieves the best average LLM-judge score on LoCoMo with both answerers.
With gpt-4.1-mini, it reaches 81.5, surpassing Nemori by 2.1 points and Full Context by 0.9 points.
With gpt-4o-mini, it reaches 77.4, exceeding Nemori by 3.0 points and Full Context by 5.1 points.
The largest LLM-judge gain over Nemori is on Temporal Reasoning, where Mem++ scores 81.4 and 76.9, which is 3.8 and 5.9 points higher.
We attribute this to the recency slots, which reserve part of the context for the latest-dated matching documents.
blocks.zh:

我们将此归因于调整档位,该档位为最新的匹配文件保留部分上下文.

Performance on Long Contexts. LongMemEval S {}_{\text{S}} conversations exceed 100K tokens, an order of magnitude more than LoCoMo ( Nan et al., 2025 ) .
On this benchmark, Mem g ++ achieves the best average with both answerers.
It reaches 72.4 with gpt-4o-mini, 4.4 points above Zep, and 75.3 with gpt-4.1-mini, 0.7 points above Nemori.
Mem++ ranks second with 72.2 and 74.7, and both variants exceed Full Context by at least 9.1 points.
Moreover, the two variants hold the top two positions on Knowledge Update and Single-session User with both answerers.

此外,两个变体在"知识更新"和"单会话用户"上占据前两个位置,两个回答者都担任.

Where Mem++ Trails. Mem++ does not lead every category.
On OrgMemBench, RAG exceeds Mem++ on Contradiction by 28.2 and 27.4 points and on Bi-temporal with gpt-4.1-mini by 16.7 points.
In addition, every method stays below 23 on Justification Chain.
On LongMemEval S {}_{\text{S}} , Mem++ trails on Temporal Reasoning with both answerers, and Nemori leads Single-session Preference with gpt-4.1-mini (86.7 vs. 47.8).
We attribute the preference gap to Nemori’s distillation, which can infer preferences that are rarely seen.
On LoCoMo, Mem++ also trails Nemori on Temporal F1 with gpt-4.1-mini (41.7 vs. 57.7).
However, the two methods are level with gpt-4o-mini (56.9 vs. 56.7), suggesting that the gap stems from answers phrasing rather than retrieval.

Write-Time Processing. Mem++ performs as well without consolidation or the fact index as with them, which shows that its accuracy does not depend on LLM calls at write time.
Indexing each original document whole also scores 2.6 points higher on LoCoMo than indexing extracted facts, even though the answerer reads the same original documents in both variants.

blocks.en: 5 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 5 结论

blocks.en:
We have argued for a non-destructive view of organizational memory, where each document is kept whole rather than distilled at write time.
Mem++ follows this view by keeping every version in one store and deferring the choice between versions to read time.
Experiments show that this design outperforms write-time extraction on OrgMemBench, achieves the best average LLM-judge score on LoCoMo and remains competitive on LongMemEval S {}_{\text{S}} .
Ablations further show that semantic retrieval over original documents drives these results, whereas consolidation, fact extraction and an entity graph add cost without a consistent gain.
These findings suggest that keeping the original documents and choosing among them at read time is a strong baseline for organizational memory.
we acknowledge that few public benchmarks target organizational memory, so our organizational evaluation rests on the 73 questions that OrgMemBench asks about one synthetic organization.
In future work, we will collect more diverse organizational records and test Mem++ on them to improve the system in this setting.
blocks.zh:
我们主张对组织记忆采取无损的观点,即每个文件保存完整,而不是在写作时提取。
Mem++遵循这个观点,将每个版本保留在一个商店中,并推迟在版本之间选择阅读时间.
实验显示,这种设计在OrgMem Bench上的写-时间提取效果优于OrgMem Bench,在LoCoMo上实现了最佳平均LLM裁判分数,在LongMemEval S QQText{S}}上仍然具有竞争力.
说明还表明,对原始文档的语义检索推动了这些结果,而合并、事实提取和实体图则增加了成本,没有取得一致的收益。
这些调查结果表明,保存原始文件并在阅读时加以选择是组织记忆的有力基准。
我们承认,很少公共基准以组织记忆为目标,因此我们的组织评估依赖于OrgMem Bench对一个合成组织提出的73个问题。
在今后的工作中,我们将收集更加多样化的组织记录,并测试Mem++,以便在这一背景下改进系统。

Unlike memories that run a language model on every incoming document ( Chhikara et al., 2025 ; Rasmussen et al., 2025 ; Xu et al., 2026 ) , 𝒞 \mathcal{C} runs between writes and queries over documents already stored.
It spends a model call only where two documents likely describe the same fact.
The operator first greedily groups current rows, where each group takes the rows whose embeddings have a cosine similarity of at least τ \tau to its first row.
It then asks a language model what changed within each group B B and assigns the group a label y ⁡ ( B ) ∈ { conflict , restatement , distinct } , y(B)\in\{\textsc{conflict},\ \textsc{restatement},\ \textsc{distinct}\}, (6) where a conflict means one fact took a new value over time, a restatement means the rows say the same thing in different words, and distinct means the rows only look alike.
In a conflict, the row with the latest event date stays current.
Each older row keeps its text and date and is marked in σ \sigma as superseded by that row, and it therefore remains retrievable with its own date.
In a restatement, a second model call writes one merged row of at most 220 tokens.
This row takes the earliest date in B B and lists every original author.
The originals are marked as archived in σ \sigma , which removes them from retrieval.
These merged rows are the only rows in the store whose text a model has written.
Because of this earliest date, a merged row can carry text from later rows past the as-of date θ \theta .
This affects only the consolidation ablation, since consolidation is off by default.
A distinct group is left untouched, and so is any group whose labeling call fails.
The cost is therefore at most two model calls per group rather than one per document.

blocks.en: B.1 Baselines
blocks.zh: B.1 基线

blocks.en: Full Context places the whole history in the prompt of the answering model and uses no external memory.
blocks.zh: Full Context将整个历史置于答题模型的提示中,并且没有使用外部内存.

blocks.en:
RAG ( Lewis et al., 2020 ; Karpukhin et al., 2020 ) splits the history into fixed-size chunks and returns the chunks whose embeddings are closest to the question.
On LoCoMo, the suffix gives the chunk size in tokens.
Unlike Mem++, it can split one document across several chunks.
blocks.zh:
RAG(Lewis等人,2020年;Karpukhin等人,2020年)将历史分成固定大小块,并返回嵌入最接近问题的块.
在 LoCoMo 上,后缀以符号给出块大小.
与Mem++不同的是,它可以将一个文档分割成多个块.

blocks.en:
Mem0 ( Chhikara et al., 2025 ) uses an LLM to extract salient facts from each new message and compares each fact with the most similar stored memories.
An LLM then adds, updates or deletes a memory or leaves the store unchanged, so a newer fact can overwrite an older one.
blocks.zh:
Mem0(Chhikara等人,2025年)使用LLM从每个新消息中提取显著的事实,并将每个事实与存储最相似的记忆进行比较.
LLM之后会添加,更新或删除一个内存或使商店保持不变,因此一个较新的事实可以覆盖一个较旧的.

blocks.en:
Zep ( Rasmussen et al., 2025 ) builds a temporal knowledge graph with its Graphiti engine.
It extracts entities and facts from each episode and stores each fact as an edge with the period over which it held.
When a later fact contradicts an edge, Zep invalidates that edge.
At query time it combines semantic, keyword and graph search over facts, entities and communities.
blocks.zh:
Zep(Rasmussen等人,2025年)用它的Graphiti引擎构建了时间知识图.
它从每一集中提取实体和事实,并将每个事实作为它所持时期的边缘。
当一个后来的事实与一个边缘相矛盾时,泽普使那个边缘无效.
在查询时,它将语义、关键词和图表搜索结合到事实、实体和社区上。

blocks.en:
A-Mem ( Xu et al., 2026 ) follows the Zettelkasten method and stores each interaction as a note with keywords, tags and a context description written by an LLM.
It links each new note to related notes and can update the attributes of older notes as new ones arrive.
blocks.zh:
A-Mem(Xu等人,2026年)遵循Zettelkasten方法,将每个交互作为备注存储,其中包含关键词,标记和一个LLM编写的上下文描述.
它将每个新注释与相关注释联系起来,并可随着新注释的到来更新旧注释的属性.

blocks.en:
Nemori ( Nan et al., 2025 ) segments a conversation into coherent episodes and rewrites each episode as a narrative.
It then distills semantic knowledge by predicting a new episode from existing memory and storing what the prediction missed.
blocks.zh:
尼莫里(Nan et al.,2025)将一段对话分为连贯的剧集,并将每集改写为叙事.
然后通过从现有的记忆中预测出新的一集,并储存预测所遗漏的东西,来提炼语义知识.

blocks.en:
gbrain ( Gardner, 2026 ) is an open-source memory system that combines keyword, vector and graph search over a store extracted from its documents.
We report it only on OrgMemBench, whose paper also evaluates it.

blocks.en: B.3 Implementation Details
blocks.zh: B.3 执行细节

blocks.en:
Table 6 lists the retrieval settings that differ across benchmarks.
All runs share the fusion constant γ = 60 \gamma=60 , k = 50 k=50 retrieved rows and three recency slots.
A disjunctive lexical index returns rows that match any query term, whereas a conjunctive one returns only rows that contain every term.
On OrgMemBench the encoder runs locally and embeds at most 256 word pieces of each document, while the stored text and the lexical index keep the full document.
Only the 15 Audit Replay questions of OrgMemBench carry an as-of date, so the date bound applies only to them.
On OrgMemBench the benchmark passes only the first 40,000 characters of the retrieved context to the answering model, and these hold about 19 of the 50 rows.
The recency slots and the Mem g ++ triples come after the fused rows, so they never reach the answering model on this benchmark.
Mem g ++ calls gpt-4o-mini twice per document at write and once per question at read.
On the conversational benchmarks, its write calls run per ten-turn chunk instead of per document.
